note: The frozen extension contract, one entry per manifest generation and one per contribution SPI generation. A generation listed here is still promised: a package built against it installs, activates, upgrades, disables, reactivates and uninstalls on this release. Anything that was once promised and is not any more is recorded under `withdrawn` rather than being deleted, because an author needs to know a surface is gone, not merely find it missing. `tools/verify-extension-contract.php` recomputes every `surface_digest` from the entry it belongs to, so changing what a generation promises fails the build until the change is made deliberately.

statuses.frozen: Still promised. The surface is closed: it may gain a new generation beside it, but this entry does not change.
statuses.withdrawn: No longer promised. Recorded so an author who built against it learns that it went, and when.

key_statuses.interpreted: The platform reads the key and acts on it.
key_statuses.advisory: The platform reads the key only to describe the package, and acts on nothing in it.
key_statuses.accepted_uninterpreted: The parser still accepts the key so older packages keep installing, and nothing reads it.

signing.note: A fixture key, deliberately derived from a written stem rather than generated, so the compatibility packages can be rebuilt and re-signed by anyone and no key material of any kind — not even the public half — is committed as a literal. It proves the signing and trust path, not provenance: the package digest is signed with `PackageSigner`, the sidecar is a `SignatureDocument`, and admission runs through `PackageTrustPolicy` over `SodiumEd25519Verifier` — the same three the platform uses for a real release key. A release key proves provenance and lives outside the repository.

host_services.note: The complete set of host services an extension may resolve from the container it is handed. The composition root allowlists these and nothing else, so a package that resolves anything absent from this list fails closed at runtime. Their identifiers are frozen; the method surface behind each is classified public but is not byte-pinned at this generation.

manifest_generations.promise: A package declares its identity, its runtime requirements, its autoload map, its migrations and its assets, and ships a provider that may register its own services, boot, and declare its own routes. It contributes nothing to the shared contribution registries and is never asked to: a schema-1 provider that implements the contribution contract is refused rather than reinterpreted. Unknown manifest keys are tolerated at this generation, which is exactly why schema 2 closed them.

Everything schema 1 promises, plus typed contributions through contribution SPI 1: capabilities, resource policies and the administrator shell — workspaces, navigation, routes and views. The manifest becomes closed to unknown keys at every level whose key set is known, so a misspelled field fails the install instead of being silently ignored, and `permissions` must match the contributed capability identifiers exactly, order included. A schema-2 provider must implement the contribution contract, and the registrar holds it to what the manifest declared: it may register nothing it did not declare and omit nothing it did.

Everything schema 2 promises, plus the three business keys schema 3 opened on the same contribution SPI 1: safe field presentation, custom business view handlers and custom business action handlers. A package may declare its own field types and present them through the markup-free presenter contract, and may answer a declared view or action contract with its own handler. The schema-2 grammar is unchanged underneath, which is why a schema-2 package does not have to move to gain anything here.

Everything schema 3 promises, on contribution SPI 2 rather than SPI 1, plus the two top-level keys SPI 2 opened: `integration` and `interface`. Durable integration is the substance of the generation — versioned event contracts, synchronous domain listeners, queue-backed consumers, jobs, queues, schedules, rebuildable projections, reports, outbound webhook adapters and money rate providers — and `interface` binds every graphical route the package mounts to a declared semantic surface. SPI 2 is fail-closed about that binding: a schema-4 package that mounts a graphical GET route without declaring its surface is refused.

spi_generations.promise: The declaration grammar and the registrar a schema-2 or schema-3 package contributes through. A manifest on either schema must declare `contributions.version` as 1; any other value is refused rather than interpreted. The export bytes of a schema-2 and schema-3 contribution set are part of this generation, which is why the constant stays at 1 even though the current SPI is 2.

Everything SPI 1 carries, plus the durable integration surfaces, the KIS semantic surface registrar and the money rate-provider registrar. A schema-4 manifest must declare `contributions.version` as 2. The two additive registrars are feature-detected rather than assumed: a provider that publishes semantic surfaces or exchange rates checks for the registrar it needs, so a provider written against the base registrar keeps working unchanged.

withdrawn.reason: It had no implementer and no caller. The lifecycle an extension observes is the platform's, driven through `ExtensionManager`, and nothing was ever going to be handed this interface.
It had no implementer and no caller. Registry reads reachable to a package go through the restricted container's allowlisted services, not through a registry port.
